verses.text: The Levitical priests, along with the whole tribe of Levi, will have no share of the land or inheritance with Israel. They’ll eat from Yahweh’s offerings given through fire and from what belongs to him.
They’ll have no inheritance among their fellow Israelites. Yahweh is their inheritance, just as he told them.
Here’s the priests’ share from anyone who brings a sacrifice of an ox or a sheep: give the priest the shoulder, both cheeks, and the inner parts.
Give him the first of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool you shear from your sheep.
Yahweh your God chose him out of all your tribes to stand and serve in Yahweh’s name, him and his sons forever.
If a Levite from any town in Israel where he lives wants with all his heart to go to the place Yahweh chooses,
he can serve in the name of Yahweh his God, just like his fellow Levites who stand there before Yahweh.
He’ll get the same share of food as they do, in addition to whatever he gets from selling his family property.
When you enter the land Yahweh your God gives you, don’t learn to copy the detestable practices of those nations.
Nobody among you may pass their son or daughter through the fire, practice divination, tell fortunes, cast spells, or practice sorcery.
Nobody may work charms, consult a familiar spirit, practice wizardry, or seek answers from the dead.
Yahweh finds anyone who does these things detestable. It’s because of these practices that Yahweh your God is driving those nations out ahead of you.
Be blameless before Yahweh your God.
The nations you’re taking the land from listen to sorcerers and diviners. Yahweh your God hasn’t given you permission to do that.
Yahweh your God will raise up a prophet like me from among your own people. Listen to him.
That’s what you asked Yahweh your God for at Horeb on the day you all gathered. You said, “Don’t let me hear Yahweh my God’s voice again or see this huge fire again, or I’ll die.”
Yahweh told me, “They’re right in what they’ve said.
I’ll raise up a prophet like you from among their own people. I’ll put my words in his mouth. He’ll tell them everything I command him.
If anyone refuses to listen to the words he speaks in my name, I’ll hold that person accountable.
But if a prophet dares to say something in my name that I never told him to say, or speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die.”
You might wonder, “How can we tell if Yahweh didn’t say something?”
If a prophet speaks in Yahweh’s name and what he says doesn’t come true, Yahweh didn’t say it. The prophet spoke on his own authority. Don’t be afraid of him.
